meta.title: NYC Ferry departure board — hardcoded NYC Ferry data
meta.description: Every piece of NYC Ferry data this repository carries that did not come from a published GTFS feed. Each section names the file it was read from; edit that file, not this one.
meta.scope: NYC Ferry only. The partner operators sharing these docks have their own hand-maintained data in this repository — NY Waterway route corrections, transcribed timetables for the Governors Island, IKEA and Liberty Landing boats, and downloads for the Staten Island Ferry and the Statue of Liberty boats — and none of it is included here. Partner stop ids and partner on/off switches are stripped from the config below.
meta.readOnly: A snapshot for export. Nothing in the build reads this file back, so editing it changes nothing.

landings.description: Every landing the board can show, keyed by the landing number an agent dials. stopIds are NYC Ferry GTFS stops. Landing 27 (Pier C) is virtual — no feed contains the home port — so it carries its own coordinates and a stop id that exists only in this repository. A landing marked nycFerryCalls: false is a real dock that NYC Ferry does not serve: its departures all belong to partner operators, so it has no NYC Ferry stop id and carries its own coordinates.

display.description: Which landing a kiosk shows and how much of it. A deployed staff or mobile server answers for every landing and uses landingNumber only as its default. busesEnabled keeps or drops connecting shuttle-bus routes, which for NYC Ferry means the Rockaway shuttles at landing 18.

crewShuttles.description: Crew shuttles, the home port, the holiday list and the thresholds used to spot a boat going out of service. None of this is published anywhere: the GTFS feed and the schedule workbook are both silent about moves made with no passengers aboard, so this file is maintained by hand and must be revisited whenever the schedule changes.

config.note: Crew shuttles and home-port runs for NYC Ferry boats. Nothing here comes from the GTFS feed or the schedule workbook - both are silent about out-of-service moves - so this file is maintained by hand and must be revisited whenever the schedule changes. See ferryAssignments.md.

outOfService.note: How a boat going out of service is spotted. The workbook marks nothing, so it is inferred from holes in a boat's own run of trips. In the bundled schedule ordinary layovers reach 44 minutes and the next gap up is 90, so 60 sits in an empty valley between them - that valley is a property of this schedule, not a law, so re-check these when the schedule changes. Gaps at or above certainAfterMinutes mean the boat leaves and the Pier C run is shown; shorter ones are marked with a question mark instead, because an hour and a half at Rockaway is more likely a crew break with the boat tied up where it is.

holidays.note: Dates that run the WEEKEND shuttle set even though the GTFS feed runs weekday service. calendar_dates.txt is empty, so the feed itself has no idea a holiday is happening - this list is the only source. Weekend-falling holidays are left out because they change nothing. Starting list only: confirm against the operator's holiday service before relying on it.

shuttles.note: One entry is one departure to the home port carrying the crews being relieved off the boats listed. 'landing' is a key in config/landings.json. 'boats' is the route code plus boat number, the same label the board badges - a boat named here is swapping crew, not finishing, so it is never marked out of service on account of the shuttle.

config.confirmationNote: These historical times remain unconfirmed. Verified ordinary fall weekday operations are supplied separately by schedules/fall-2026-weekday-crew.json. Weekend and Sukkot crew data remain unconfirmed.

crewModelConstants.description: The constants the out-of-service model runs on. These are inference parameters, not published facts, and each was chosen against the shape of the bundled schedule — re-check them when the schedule changes.

homePortStopId.note: Pier C is in no feed, so the virtual landing's one stop id exists only in this repository.

crewServiceIds.note: Synthetic calendars. The feed's own weekday service cannot be reused, because on a holiday the feed still runs weekdays while the crews change on the weekend pattern.

crewRoute.note: A crew shuttle belongs to no passenger route; borrowing one's colour would imply the boat is running that service.

crewSwapWindowBefore.note: How long before a boat's run ends a listed shuttle may be and still be read as the cause of the gap.

crewSwapWindowAfter.note: And how long after. A crew rides the shuttle shortly after stepping off, not six hours into a gap.

shuttleReadyBefore.note: A shuttle is listed at the minute it is ready and then waits for the boat to sail, so it can appear well before the crew it collects has finished. Bounded empirically: the widest real case in the bundled config is 31 minutes.

boatAssignments.description: GTFS trip_short_name to the numbered boat that works it, imported from the seasonal workbook by scripts/import-boat-assignments.py. This is what lets the board label a sailing 'ER5', infer where a boat stops working, and predict the vessel on a sailing the feed has not reached.

boatShifts.description: Published crew shift boundaries, imported from the workbook's cell notes by scripts/import-boat-shifts.py and verified against the bundled GTFS at import time — anything the feed disagreed with was dropped rather than guessed at.

RR1.source: supplied by hand 2026-08-13 (RWY RKT column is unreadable)

fleet.description: The vessel roster. Used to turn a realtime vehicle label into a name a person recognises; each record carries only the id, name and hull number the match runs on.
